signals.title: Pecco Bagnaia: «Ich bin nicht der Typ, der so etwas in die Kamera sagt»

Wie es ihm geht und was es in Silverstone braucht, um zu gewinnen. MotoGP 06.08.2026 - 17:01

signals.title: Kawasaki announces four-strong Ninja 2027 line-up
signals.summary: Kawasaki has revealed the latest version of the ZX-6R, with the 2027 model set to arrive in three colourways and with styling inspired by the ZX-10R. Kawasaki has revealed a new four-model Ninja line-up for 2027, which features the latest version of the ZX-6R. The ZX-6R will continue to be joined by the Ninja ZX-4R, and the more track-focused ZX-4RR, as part of a mid-to-low-capacity supersport segment that has grown into one of the most congested across all two-wheel categories at the moment, especially with regards to racing. For example, the World Supersport Championship was previously dominated by machinery such as the Yamaha R6 and Kawasaki’s ZX-6R, however, bigger and more powerful machines such as the Yamaha R9, Ducati Panigale V2 and ZXMoto 820RR-RS are enjoying the most success, currently. Following a brief hiatus in 2020, the ZX-6R has been a staple of the brand’s supersport range since, and it makes use of race-derived chassis and styling inspired by the company’s flagship Ninja ZX-10R. The new model will also be available in three colourways, including a Metallic Matte Carbon Gray/Metallic Spark Black, which is our favourite of the bunch. The new model once again features the company’s famed 636cc inline-four engine, and produces maximum power of 127.6 bhp at 13,000rpm and 50.8 Ib-ft of torque at 10,800rpm. signals.title: Holy stolen motorcycles! Mexico's caped crusader is cleaning up the streets
signals.summary: A mystery vigilante dubbed 'Batman' has become an unlikely folk hero in Mexico after allegedly hunting down suspected motorcycle thieves and leaving them taped to lampposts. Forget the Batmobile, batarangs and billion-dollar gadgets; Mexico's answer to Batman appears to rely on little more than duct tape and a marker pen. The mystery vigilante has become an overnight internet sensation after allegedly tracking down suspected motorcycle thieves in the Mexican city of Lagos de Moreno, before leaving them humiliated and taped to lampposts alongside the bikes they were accused of stealing. Over the course of around 10 days, at least five alleged thieves have reportedly been found bound to street poles, some with the Spanish word 'ratero' (thief) written across their foreheads, complete with cartoon moustaches and cat whiskers. In several cases, the recovered motorcycles were left parked directly in front of the suspects, seemingly as evidence of their alleged crimes. The anonymous crime-fighter has quickly been christened the "Batman of Lagos de Moreno" on social media, where plenty of users have praised the masked vigilante for doing what they believe local authorities have failed to do amid a rise in motorcycle thefts. Authorities, however, are rather less enthusiastic.
